summary:
This review explains how caller scope can promote existing GitHub work without starting a second operation.

- Shared reads connect callers to one work scope and manage cancellation for each reader.
- Work scopes carry promotions across asynchronous calls and into pending scheduler entries.
- The scheduler selects pending work by current priority. The client retries paced work outside a network slot.

This is current code, not a proposed change. Active requests are not preempted. The scheduler does not itself enforce rate limits.
riskRationale: Shared mutable scopes connect request priority, concurrency, and cancellation. An incorrect connection can delay interactive work or cancel work that another reader still needs.
storyArc: Follow an interactive caller into existing shared work. Show how the caller updates the work scope, how pending requests read that scope, and how paced work returns to scheduling. Keep reader cancellation separate from work priority.

topics.title: Interactive callers promote shared work through its live scope
topics.narrativeBrief: How does an interactive caller promote existing work through caller scope, shared reads, and scheduling? Connect the supplied shared-read path to mutable work scopes and client rescheduling; verify the omitted inflight lookup and pacing decision before showing their exact paths.

diagramBrief.question: How does an interactive caller make existing work eligible for interactive scheduling without replacing that work?
diagramBrief.takeaway: A joining caller raises the shared work scope. Pending tasks that retain this scope use its current effective priority at the next scheduling opportunity. Active requests continue, and paced work sleeps outside a scheduler slot before it tries again.
essentialConcepts: AsyncLocalStorage supplies the caller scope; the default priority is foreground.
createSharedGitHubRead starts one GitHubWork and calls joinGitHubWork before shared.read.
joinGitHubWork raises the work scope priority rather than creating another operation. An interactive promotion also makes the work non-automatic.
createGitHubWork retains a parent scope. Effective priority follows higher parent priorities, including after an await.
Shared readers have separate cancellation. The shared controller aborts only when the last reader leaves before settlement.
The scheduler retains a supplied scope object and reads effective priority when draining pending tasks.
Pending interactive work precedes foreground work; background work follows when neither is pending.
Only tasks marked parallel with current interactive priority can use parallel admission. The scheduler allows at most three active tasks; exclusive work blocks further starts.
The client schedules with githubPriorityScope(). A paced result causes a short sleep outside the slot, then another scheduling attempt.
Client code owns pacing and budget handling. The scheduler owns pending selection and concurrency, not rate-limit enforcement.
